title: Chaos in reason: How chain-of-thought LLMs can look for an answer
authors: Gregorio Jaca, Kristóf Benedek, János Török
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet their internal dynamics remain poorly understood. In this work, we apply the tools of nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory to LLMs. By analyzing both text and hidden state trajectories, we demonstrate that LLMs exhibit hallmark signatures of chaos, including strong sensitivity to initial conditions, manifested as intermittent, jump-like divergence of nearby trajectories combined with bounded evolution, with consistent results across different distance metrics. An exact Jacobian analysis of the Transformer's sub-blocks shows that self-attention and the feed-forward network expand and propagate perturbations, while normalization and residual connections counteract this expansion and promote stability. Recurrence plots show structural similarities between LLMs and canonical chaotic systems such as the Lorenz attractor, while dimension analysis reveals fractal structures in the hidden state space, particularly pronounced in the last layers. We propose that the nonlinear coupling induced by attention mechanisms plays a key role in driving this chaotic behavior.
summary: This work applies chaos theory tools to analyze the internal dynamics of Large Language Models (LLMs), treating them as nonlinear dynamical systems. The authors demonstrate that LLMs exhibit clear signatures of deterministic chaos, linking this behavior to the non-linear coupling within attention mechanisms. This provides a novel theoretical framework for understanding model interpretability and information processing in deep learning.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the internal dynamics of Large Language Models (LLMs) by determining if their reasoning process exhibits signatures characteristic of deterministic chaos.
main_result: LLMs exhibit hallmark signatures of chaos, driven primarily by the nonlinear coupling induced within the self-attention mechanisms. The analysis suggests that the effective dynamical state requires considering temporal dependencies across the context window rather than just the last hidden state.
method: The authors apply tools from nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory, analyzing latent-state trajectories using diagnostics like Lyapunov exponents and recurrence plots, complemented by an exact Jacobian analysis of Transformer sub-blocks.
model_or_system: The system is a Large Language Model based on the Transformer architecture, viewed as a discrete-time dynamical system during autoregressive token generation. Analysis compares dynamics in hidden-state space versus sentence embedding space.
key_observables: Sensitivity to initial conditions (divergence), recurrence plot structures (e.g., Lorenz attractor similarity), fractal dimensions ($D_2$), and the anisotropic expansion factor ($ ar{\lambda}$).
important_parameters: The perturbation magnitude ($\Delta(k)$) used for trajectory divergence, and the size of the sliding window used to smooth temporal measurements.
main_assumptions: Mean-field derivations rely on approximations like neglecting off-diagonal cross-terms in the Jacobian norm squared. The analysis also assumes that local encoding is captured by increasing the sliding window size.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate recurrence plots comparing periodic, chaotic (Lorenz), and random motion; divergence curves using Hausdorff distance comparing noisy window-free vs. smoothed windowed measurements; and correlation dimensions of embedding matrices.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies chaos diagnostics to LLM dynamics, first analyzing trajectory divergences across different metrics, then performing operator-level Jacobian analysis on components (attention/FFN), and finally distinguishing between local hidden-state dynamics and context-aware sentence embeddings using windowing techniques.
why_interesting: By framing the complex computation of an LLM as a high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system, it provides a theoretical lens to analyze emergent computational properties, drawing parallels with established concepts in chaotic physical systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
